questions.question: Which column type is the right choice for storing order amounts in INR?
options: FLOAT, because it is compact and fast
DOUBLE, because it has more precision than FLOAT
DECIMAL(12,2), because it stores exact fixed-point values
VARCHAR(20), so the value is never rounded
questions.explanation: FLOAT and DOUBLE are binary floating point and cannot represent most decimal fractions exactly; DECIMAL stores exact values, which money requires.

questions.question: What is the key behavioural difference between DATETIME and TIMESTAMP in MySQL?
options: TIMESTAMP is converted to UTC on write and back to the session time_zone on read, and is limited to 2038; DATETIME is stored as given
DATETIME is converted to UTC; TIMESTAMP is stored exactly as given
There is no difference other than storage size
TIMESTAMP supports dates up to 9999-12-31, DATETIME only to 2038
questions.explanation: TIMESTAMP is a 32-bit epoch value with time-zone conversion and a 2038-01-19 upper bound; DATETIME has no conversion and a range up to 9999-12-31.

questions.question: A column declared with the character set `utf8` rejects an emoji. Why?
options: In MySQL `utf8` is an alias for utf8mb3, which allows at most 3 bytes per character, and emoji need 4
questions.explanation: MySQL's legacy utf8 is utf8mb3; only utf8mb4 (the 8.0 default) can store 4-byte characters such as emoji.

questions.question: What does the 11 in `INT(11)` control in MySQL 8.0?
options: The maximum number of digits that can be stored
The number of bytes used for storage
Only a deprecated display width; it does not change range or storage
questions.explanation: Integer display width is deprecated since 8.0.17 and has no effect on the value range; INT is always 4 bytes.
